open_points.subject: Disclosure-class ordering
open_points.text: “the members and the order have that one home” in `models`, but `canonical_values` also “Owns ... The order of disclosure classes”
open_points.question: Does `models` own the disclosure-class order while `canonical_values` only applies it, or does `canonical_values` own the order too?
options: `models` owns the enumeration and order; `canonical_values` owns only highest-class computation
`canonical_values` owns both the order and highest-class computation
Split declaration and operational ordering between the two modules
open_points.default_guess: `models` owns the enumeration and order; `canonical_values` reads that order to compute the highest class.

open_points.subject: Equal-content submission behavior
open_points.text: `canonical_values` “Owns A01 rules 1 and 4,” although rule 4 says an existing record is returned unchanged and nothing is recorded, while `canonical_values` may know neither `store` nor the domain modules
open_points.question: Which module decides and enforces the return-existing-and-record-nothing behavior for contracts, implementations, trial cases, flows and values?
options: Each owning domain module enforces it using identities from `canonical_values` and records from `store`
`store` provides one generic atomic insert-or-return-existing operation
`canonical_values` is given persistence knowledge despite the declared dependency boundary
open_points.default_guess: Each domain owner enforces the behavior, backed by an atomic store capability; `canonical_values` owns only identity computation.

open_points.subject: Randomly minted entity identifiers
open_points.text: A01 rule 2 requires `trial_execution_id`, `binding_id`, `run_id`, `approval_id` and `grant_id` to be “minted at random by the kernel,” but no State 3 module owns random identifier generation or collision handling
open_points.question: Which module generates these identifiers, and which module atomically checks and retries collisions?
options: `store` mints and collision-checks identifiers in the record-creation transaction
Each domain owner mints identifiers and asks `store` to reject collisions
A new shared identifier capability owns generation while `store` owns collision checking
open_points.default_guess: `store` mints and collision-checks each identifier atomically when creating the record.

open_points.subject: Start-up recovery of waiting runs
open_points.text: The shared rules say “the next start derives every run,” while `runs` owns only “start-up recovery of runs left `running`” and `runs.recover_running_runs` advances “the runs left `running`”
open_points.question: Must recovery re-derive stored status and waiting points for every non-ended run, including `awaiting_approval` and `pending`, before deciding which runs to advance, or inspect only runs stored as `running`?
options: Re-derive every non-ended run, repair stale status and waiting points, then advance only those derived as `running`
Recover only runs whose stored status is `running`
Use separate recovery passes for waiting-state repair and running-run advancement
open_points.default_guess: Re-derive every non-ended run first, then advance only those whose derived state is `running`.

open_points.subject: File inputs passed to service operations
open_points.text: `service_invoker` owns “building one HTTP request ... from ... the node's inputs,” including multipart file content, but its `Knows` list omits `store`, which alone provides `read_value_bytes` for a `SpooledFile`
open_points.question: Which module reads spooled file bytes, and what representation crosses into `service_invoker.prepare_request`?
options: `effects` reads the bytes through `store` and passes materialized inputs to `service_invoker`
`service_invoker` gains a dependency on `store` and resolves file references itself
`service_invoker` receives a caller-supplied byte-stream capability without knowing `store`
open_points.default_guess: `effects` reads the referenced bytes through `store` and passes bounded, materialized inputs to `service_invoker`.

open_points.subject: File inputs passed to sandbox executions
open_points.text: `sandbox.execute_function` must give Python `bytes` for file ports, but `sandbox` does not know `store`, while trial fixtures and run files are stored only behind `store.read_value_bytes`
open_points.question: Do `functions` and `runs` materialize file bytes before calling the sandbox, or may the sandbox resolve stored file references itself?
options: `functions` and `runs` read file bytes through `store` and pass materialized inputs
`sandbox` gains a dependency on `store`
The sandbox receives a byte-source capability supplied by its caller
open_points.default_guess: `functions` and `runs` materialize all file inputs through `store` before calling `sandbox.execute_function`.

open_points.subject: Pinned release dependencies and sandbox runtime
open_points.text: The text says the exact dependency versions and sandbox runtime are “a release artifact built and checked outside the running kernel,” but assigns no module or named build component to own that artifact or its verification
open_points.question: What owns the dependency lock, sandbox-runtime image or bundle, and the check that their exact versions match release v1?
options: A named release-build or packaging component outside the runtime module graph
`data_provider` owns both the version declarations and their build-time verification
`sandbox` owns the runtime bundle while the project dependency lock remains an external build concern
open_points.default_guess: A named release-build component owns the dependency lock, sandbox-runtime bundle and build-time verification; runtime `sandbox` owns only the probe.
